appraisal_events.evidence: je me trouvai si heureux, je sentais qu'elle m'avait si parfaitement débarrassé de ces clochers et de ce qu'ils cachaient derrière eux... je me mis à chanter à tue-tête
appraisal_events.explanation: The retrospective narrator frames the young narrator's successful conversion of an obscure impression into written prose as a triumphant creative release, a moment of narrator-endorsed emotional and artistic renewal.

appraisal_events.evidence: je recevais dans un baiser celui de ma mère, tout entier, sans la réserve d'une arrière-pensée... je n'aurais souhaité que vînt me dire bonsoir une mère plus belle et plus intelligente que la mienne
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator explicitly elevates his mother's love as uniquely complete and unreserved, declaring he would want no more beautiful or intelligent mother in her place, a direct comparative idealization.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator moves from obscure unease to intense joy and relief after successfully articulating his impression of the steeples in writing.
The mother is idealized by the narrator as an irreplaceable, incomparable source of complete love, set explicitly above any hypothetical substitute or later mistress.

ambiguities: The passage also contains an extended section of anticipatory dread about the mother's absence at bedtime ('j'aurais voulu mourir'), which could be read as a negative emotional movement for the narrator; it is not represented as a separate event because it describes a recurring anxious state rather than a discrete evaluative act by or toward a named character.
